subject: Clarification: Dedicated reserved pool — excess usage, throttles, and billing options

Subject: Clarify Dedicated pool overages & billing model

Laura / Aditya,

Thanks for the demo earlier. We are evaluating a Reserved (Dedicated) GPU pool for FinEdge's realtime scoring workload and have a couple of questions that are blocking procurement:

1) If we exceed our monthly committed vGPU-hours, how is excess usage billed? Is it per-token, per-vGPU-hour, or a blended per-minute metering?

2) Do you enforce hard throttles when commit is exceeded or do you allow bursting and bill after (we prefer predictable behavior)?

3) Can you provide examples of how you size a pool for target throughput (e.g., 50 requests/sec 1k tokens average) so we can validate the commit size?

4) Are there built-in mitigations (auto-fallback to smaller models, transparent rate-limits, or grace credits) to avoid sudden outages?

We have a budget constraint and want a model that avoids surprise invoices. If there are options (buffer credits, pre-purchased burst packs, or tiered overage discounts) we'd like to see them.

Attached: monthly_usage_sample.csv (sanitized usage for June).

Appreciate a written summary we can attach to our SOW.

Best,
Alex
Alex Morgan
Head of ML Infrastructure, FinEdge Solutions

Subject: Re: Clarify Dedicated pool overages & billing model

Alex — thanks for the clear list. I pulled together how Redwood handles reserved commits, overage, and practical mitigations so you can include it in procurement and the SOW. Summary below, followed by concrete options we can put in the quote.

Short answers up front:
- Metering: Dedicated usage is metered at a per-minute granularity and normalized to "vGPU-hours". We convert service-level throughput (tokens/sec) to vGPU consumption using our model-backed profiles.
- Overage behavior: By default we allow bursting above commit for short windows and bill overage at a higher per-vGPU-hour rate. For customers who require budget predictability we offer (A) hard-cap mode with automatic request rejections, or (B) pre-purchased burst credits that cap invoice exposure.
- Mitigations: automatic soft-fallback to a lower-cost model, configurable throttling thresholds, and optional buffer-credit pools.

Detailed notes (for SOW):
1) Sizing
- We map your expected QPS and token distribution to a recommended commit in vGPU-hours. Example: for ~50 requests/sec at ~1k tokens average and using a moderate Llama-4-like model, that maps to roughly 8 vGPUs sustained (estimate) with headroom for burst windows. We'll validate with a short proof-of-load run.

2) Metering & billing units
- Billing unit: normalized vGPU-minute (1 vGPU-minute = 1/60 of a vGPU-hour). Tokens are not billed directly for Dedicated; they drive vGPU consumption in the normalization.
- Metering interval: 1-minute rolling window, aggregated per-customer, exported in the usage CSV (similar to the sample you shared).

3) Overage handling options
Option 1 — Default (burst + bill):
  - Short bursts allowed, billed at overage rate (base_rate * 1.8).
  - Monthly true-up invoice for overage, line-itemized as vGPU-hours over commit.
Option 2 — Hard cap (predictable):
  - When commit is reached, additional requests receive 429/503 with a clear retry-after. No overage invoicing.
Option 3 — Burst credits (recommended for predictability + availability):
  - You pre-purchase a pool of burst credits (vGPU-hours) at a discounted overage rate. When credits are depleted, we fall back to hard-cap or lower-tier model according to policy.
Option 4 — Tiered overage discount (volume-driven):
  - If monthly overage exceeds tiers (e.g., 0-100h, 100-500h, >500h), we automatically apply step discounts on the overage rate.

4) SLAs & guarantees
- Dedicated capacity customers get a throughput SLA tied to the committed pool. If we fail to meet throughput after a validated setup run, we offer service credits. Bursting behavior is explicitly excluded from throughput SLOs unless documented as part of the commit.

5) Practical protections to avoid bill shock
- Monthly threshold alerts (50%, 75%, 90% of commit).
- Auto-policy: if projected overage > X% we can: (a) pre-notify procurement and pause burst allowing manual approval, or (b) automatically fall back to a lower-cost model per route to preserve availability.

Attachments: SOW_v2.pdf (draft language for reserved commit and billing options).

Next steps:
- I can add one of the three billing options into the quote (Default, Hard cap, Burst credits) — which should I draft?
- Aditya can run a quick sizing confirmation if you share a 24h live trace.

Thanks,

- For Option 3, can you confirm whether burst credits expire monthly or can be banked across months? We'd prefer banked credits to smooth seasonal spikes.
- On discounts: if we increase our committed pool by 20% mid-term, can we get prorated pricing and apply the higher discount to future months (not retroactive)?

Alex — quick technical note to make the sizing more concrete for your engineering team.

1) Sizing example math (conservative):
  - Measured: 1 vGPU (A100-class) serving our mix handles ~12-15 requests/sec with 1k tokens avg for the model profile we validated.
  - So 50 req/sec sustained -> ~4.5 vGPUs sustained (we round up to 5) + 2 vGPUs buffer for peaks -> recommended commit 7 vGPUs.
  - Convert to vGPU-hours: 7 vGPUs * 24h * 30d ≈ 5040 vGPU-hours/month.

2) Burst handling patterns
  - Short spikes (minutes): allowed and metered. If spikes are sustained beyond a configurable burst window (default 30 minutes aggregated), we either begin throttling or consume pre-purchased burst credits.
  - We can configure the burst-window per-customer when the contract is signed (examples: 10m/30m/60m).

3) Billing semantics & invoicing
  - Overages are invoiced on the following month's bill with line items showing minute-by-minute normalized usage (CSV).
  - Burst credit pools can be purchased with a 12-month shelf-life by default; multi-year customers can bank across contract years under enterprise terms (we can reflect that in the SOW).

4) Mid-term commit increases
  - We prorate the increase for the remaining month and apply the new committed rate going forward. Discounts apply prospectively, not retroactively.

Suggested commercial language to include in SOW (short):
  "Customer may elect hard-cap or burst-credit behavior for Dedicated capacity. Burst credits purchased shall have a default 12-month shelf-life unless otherwise agreed in writing. Mid-term increases to committed capacity shall be prorated for the current billing cycle and eligible for prospective discounts per the applicable pricing table."

If you'd like, I can run the numbers for your actual June sample (attached) and give a tailored commit recommendation.

–Aditya

Alex / Sophie — thanks, all. Glad we're converging. Proposed next steps so procurement/legal can proceed: 

1) We will add Option 3 (Burst credits, bankable 12 months) as the default in the quote and include hard-cap behavior as an opt-out.
2) SOW_v2.pdf will be updated with the commercial clause Aditya proposed and with explicit burst-window choices (10/30/60m).
3) Pricing: we'll set the base committed vGPU-hour price in the quote and a pre-defined overage rate ladder (base * 1.8 / 1.5 / 1.2 depending on purchased tier). If you commit to a +20% increase mid-term, we'll prorate and apply discounts prospectively.
4) Legal/PO: we received procurement_PO_FinEdge_4512.pdf — our legal will review and I will loop in our contracts manager.

I'll circulate an updated quote + SOW by EOD tomorrow; please flag if you need a hard cap instead of burst credits and we'll flip the default. Also, Aditya — please run the June sample and drop us the tailored commit recommendation inline with the quote.

Thanks,
